learn.hook: Rabindranath Tagore wrote the national anthems of TWO countries — India's and Bangladesh's!
points: Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) was a poet, writer, musician and painter from Bengal, lovingly called Gurudev.
In 1913 he won the Nobel Prize in Literature — the first Asian to win a Nobel Prize.
He wrote 'Jana Gana Mana', India's national anthem.
He started a school at Santiniketan in West Bengal, which grew into Visva-Bharati University.
His poem 'Paper Boats' shows a child sending boats down a stream, dreaming they will reach faraway lands. Below is our own poem on that idea.

example.q: Read: I fold my homework sheet into a boat, / And set it on the stream where raindrops float. / I draw a smiling sun in crayon blue — / Dear stranger, will this boat sail all the way to you? What does the child hope for?
steps: The child sets the boat on a stream.
The child draws a smiling sun on it.
'Dear stranger' — the child hopes someone far away will find it.
example.answer: The child hopes the boat will travel far and reach a stranger in another place.

learn.reallife: Every time you sing 'Jana Gana Mana' in the school assembly, you are singing Tagore's words.

games.title: Tagore true or false
items: Tagore was the first Asian to win a Nobel Prize.
He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
Tagore won the Nobel Prize for science.
His Nobel Prize was in Literature.
Tagore's school there grew into Visva-Bharati University.
Tagore was a poet who never painted.
He was also a painter, especially in his later years.

games.title: Tagore's world
pairs: his book of songs linked to the Nobel Prize
the name people lovingly called him

quiz.q: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in:
quiz.explain: He won the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature.

quiz.q: In which year did Tagore win the Nobel Prize?
quiz.explain: Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the year with India's Independence or the Republic

quiz.q: Who wrote India's national anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana'?
quiz.explain: Tagore wrote it. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote 'Vande Mataram', the national song.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the national anthem with the national song

quiz.q: Santiniketan, where Tagore started his school, is in:
quiz.explain: Santiniketan is in West Bengal; the school grew into Visva-Bharati University.
quiz.mistake: Does not link Tagore with Bengal

quiz.q: 'I draw a smiling sun in crayon blue — / Dear stranger, will this boat sail all the way to you?' Who does the child hope will find the boat?
options: Someone far away whom the child has never met
The child's little brother at home
quiz.explain: 'Dear stranger' and 'all the way to you' show the child hopes someone far away, whom the child does not know, will find the boat.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect 'Dear stranger' with someone far away

quiz.q: 'Dear stranger, will this boat sail all the way to you?' A 'stranger' is:
quiz.explain: A stranger is a person you have never met.

quiz.q: 'I fold my homework sheet into a boat, / And set it on the stream where raindrops float.' Which word rhymes with 'boat'?
quiz.explain: 'Boat' and 'float' both end with the '-oat' sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that only looks similar

quiz.q: What is the main feeling in the poem about the paper boat?
quiz.explain: The child dreams the boat will reach a faraway friend — a hopeful, wondering feeling.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the mood of the poem

teach.ask: Gappu found a paper boat floating down a stream! Who was Tagore, and what is his poem 'Paper Boats' about?
teach.praise: What a dreamy poem! Maybe my boat will reach a bird in another land!
teach.nudge: What does the child in the poem dream will happen to the boats?

learn.hook: 'My dreams are kites' — can a dream really be a kite? In a poem, it can!
points: A simile compares two things using 'like' or 'as': 'The boat bobbed like a duck.'
A metaphor says one thing IS another, without 'like' or 'as': 'The stream was a silver ribbon.'
Similes and metaphors paint pictures in the reader's mind.
Common similes: as busy as a bee, as brave as a lion, as cool as a cucumber, as light as a feather.
We use 'will' to talk about future dreams: 'One day I will become a pilot.'

example.q: Simile or metaphor? (a) 'The paper boat floated like a leaf.' (b) 'Childhood is a garden of dreams.'
steps: (b) says childhood IS a garden, no 'like' or 'as' → metaphor
example.answer: (a) is a simile; (b) is a metaphor.

learn.reallife: Film songs, poems and even everyday talk ('She's a star!') are full of similes and metaphors.

games.title: Simile or metaphor?
items: He is as fast as a cheetah.
The baby slept like a log.
Books are doors to new worlds.
Dadi's lap is a soft pillow.
The moon is a silver plate.

quiz.q: 'The paper boat floated like a leaf.' This is a:
quiz.explain: It compares the boat to a leaf using 'like'.

quiz.q: 'The stream was a silver ribbon.' This is a:
quiz.explain: It says the stream IS a ribbon, without 'like' or 'as'.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every comparison is a simile

quiz.q: Complete the simile: 'as cool as a ___'
quiz.explain: 'As cool as a cucumber' means very calm.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the common simile

quiz.explain: Snow is very white, so 'as white as snow'.

options: The moon looks like a plate.
He runs as fast as the wind.
Dreams are wings that carry us far.
quiz.explain: It says dreams ARE wings — a metaphor. The others use 'like' or 'as'.

quiz.q: Which word signals that a comparison is a simile?
quiz.mistake: Does not know the signal words of a simile

quiz.q: 'Arjun dreams of becoming a pilot. One day he ___ fly planes.'
quiz.explain: 'One day' points to the future, so we use 'will'.
quiz.mistake: Uses a past form for a future dream

quiz.q: Why do poets use similes and metaphors?
options: To help readers picture things in a fresh way
quiz.explain: Comparisons create vivid pictures in the reader's mind.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about the effect on the reader

teach.ask: Gappu wants to describe his dream of flying high. What is a simile and what is a metaphor?
teach.praise: My wings are like kites! No wait — my wings ARE kites! Simile and metaphor!
